feedback.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-{10}^{x-2}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- We take the curve $y={10}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/0fae83bb6962fff7c1b182e4ba2e548a95e4fbe5527e14eb6607b905129e503e.png)

 

- Horizontally shift it by $2$ units to the right to give $y={10}^{x-2}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(2,1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/bb9d5c110388591d1965117724fe683bb0af6e45f4e3b60c95bc959b14d76afe.png)

- Then, reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-{10}^{x-2}.$ The point $(2,1)$ moves to $(2,-1)$ and the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/5cae0046253d7ebc3c93000bad49d4d0e8b3653597fcbd2f16468c679ebe0116.png)
